title: Prawn Fra Diavolo
subtitle: Spicy Italian-American prawns with tomato and chilli over linguine
excerpt: Fra diavolo means 'brother devil', a name earned by the chilli heat in this Italian-American classic. Raw prawns cook in a bold tomato sauce with plenty of garlic and chilli flakes. Serve over linguine or with crusty bread.
sourceNotes: Italian-American fra diavolo sauce with prawns, a mid-century New York red-sauce restaurant staple, adapted for home cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce can be made a day ahead. Add the prawns just before serving.

content.text: The prawns cook very fast and must come off the heat the moment they turn pink. Overcooking is the only real risk here. Build the sauce first, then add the prawns at the very end.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the linguine according to the packet. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine if using. Let it bubble for 1 minute to reduce slightly.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Season with salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce has thickened a little.
Add the prawns. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until they are just pink and curled. Do not cook further.
Add the drained linguine and a splash of pasta water. Toss everything together. Add lemon juice if using.
Scatter over the parsley. Serve at once.

items.fix: Add prawns right at the end and remove the pan from the heat as soon as they curl and turn fully pink.

items.cause: The tomatoes needed longer to reduce.
items.fix: Simmer the sauce for 5 more minutes before adding the prawns.

items.symptom: The dish is too hot to eat.
items.fix: Start with half a teaspoon and taste the sauce before adding more.
